agree.reason: The nurse's first-hand log and candid tone would persuade a sympathetic parent, but a board member who resists still has no answer on athletics and only a 'look at it' proposal for working parents, so they may stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: It rightly declines the graduation-rate promise the brief asked for, but it adds unsupported claims: that the other district hasn't had a full four-year class, that students would gain 'the hour of sleep they need', and that the AAP is 'the main professional body'.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the raw figures into useful forms: 412 is more than 198+171 combined, visits drop by more than half, 640/890 is nearly three in four, 84% means one in six doesn't finish, and 31% is 'almost a third'; it leaves the $180,000 cost unscaled (no per-student or per-visit figure).

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is shown as a cost too: 412 first-period visits and avoidable tardies repeated next year if nothing changes. The brief gives no trend data, so none is overlooked.

qualification.reason: It names the outcomes to track (tardies, attendance, nurse visits, graduation) and asks for annual public reports, but sets no target number, no date to judge by and no consequence if the later start fails.

objections.reason: The cost objection is answered by comparison, and working parents get a concrete suggestion (supervised early opening), but the athletic director's objection is handed back as homework rather than answered.

fit.reason: It is a well-built op-ed with a clear ask and a dated vote, but at roughly 660–680 words it runs slightly over the 650-word limit, and the name and school are still placeholders.
